record_notice: ORIGINAL PRACTICAL NOTE — written for this repository without outside sources. This is an original cooking note, not a demonstration record. It has not been cooked or tested by this project, has had no professional food-safety review and is not publication-ready. Use a probe thermometer to check the chicken’s centre temperature; colour alone cannot establish doneness.
summary: Boneless chicken thigh cut into bite-sized pieces and cooked at high heat until the outsides colour. Thigh tends to stay moist with an extra minute of cooking. Measure the centre of the thickest piece with a probe thermometer to check doneness.

ingredients.note: Breast fillet works if that is what is in the fridge; cut it a little larger and start checking it earlier, because it dries out faster.

ingredients.item: Paprika, garlic powder, dried oregano, salt and pepper
ingredients.note: Any supermarket seasoning blend does the same job. Check the jar for allergens.
Optional; adds acidity to the cooked chicken.

method.instruction: Cut the thigh into pieces of about 3 cm on a board you will wash straight afterwards, then toss them in a bowl with the oil and the seasoning until every piece is coated.
Set the air fryer to 200°C. Preheat only if your appliance manual calls for it.

Spread the pieces in the basket in a single layer with gaps between them. If the basket is crowded, cook in two batches. Piled-up chicken traps steam, browns poorly and heats unevenly, which can leave some pieces undercooked.

Cook for 12 to 15 minutes, shaking the basket at about 7 minutes, then measure the thickest piece with a probe thermometer. Chicken needs to reach 75°C in the centre — that is the figure these notes are written to, and because this record cites no source you should confirm it against the guidance your own food-safety authority publishes. Keep the probe in the meat and clear of the basket and any metal, which read hotter than the food. Colour and elapsed time are not tests: if it reads under 75°C, cook for another 2 minutes and measure again.

Keep raw chicken separate: wash hands, board, knife and the mixing bowl before touching cooked food, bread or salad. Never return cooked pieces to the raw-meat bowl. After cooking, switch off, unplug and let the appliance cool before cleaning. Follow its manual for removable parts, soaking and cleaning products; never immerse the electrical unit or assume water alone is enough.

yield_note: Serves 2 to 3. Editorial planning estimate: prep about 5 to 8 minutes; cook 12 to 15 minutes per batch; total about 20 minutes for one batch, excluding preheating and any extra cooking to reach the measured endpoint. A second batch adds a full 12 to 15 minutes, plus handling. Equipment: air fryer, knife and board, mixing bowl, tongs and probe thermometer. Editorial measuring convention for these original notes: tablespoon 20 mL; teaspoon 5 mL. These are volume measures, not gram conversions.

caveats: Cook the chicken until a probe thermometer reads 75°C at the centre of the thickest piece, with the probe clear of the basket and any metal. Chicken can remain undercooked after the stated time or after the outside has browned; measure its centre temperature.

A probe thermometer is required; do not validate chicken by colour or by cutting it open. There is no no-thermometer fallback here. Confirm the provisional endpoint in these uncited notes against the applicable local authority’s poultry guidance before cooking.
Raw chicken contaminates whatever it touches. Use a board you wash immediately, wash your hands, and keep cooked pieces away from anything the raw meat sat on.
Thaw frozen chicken fully before it goes in. A 500 g pile of part-frozen pieces will not heat evenly, and the outside will be done long before the middle.
These are practical notes, untested by this project and never given a professional food-safety review. They are not a substitute for the food-safety guidance published where you live.
